metadata.note: LA Metro Rail (A, B, C, D, E, K lines), as of the GTFS feed pulled from https://gitlab.com/LACMTA/gtfs_rail. Route geometry, frequency (headway_min, from real scheduled trip counts on a representative Wednesday, Aug 26 2026), and avg_speed_kmh (from real scheduled trip duration) are all sourced directly from the agency's own GTFS feed, same methodology as data/amtrak.geojson and data/rtd_denver_light_rail.geojson. Historical segments (pre-2026) were added from Metro's own line-opening and rebranding history: the 1990 Blue Line (LA's first modern light rail since the old Pacific Electric network), the 1993 Red Line subway (LA's first subway) and its 2006 Purple Line split, the 1995 Green Line, the 2003/2016 Gold Line and its Azusa extension, the 2012/2016 Expo Line to Santa Monica, the 2021 systemwide rename from colors to letters, the June 2023 Regional Connector (which physically joined the old Blue/Gold/Expo Lines through a new downtown tunnel into today's through-routed A and E Lines), and the 2022 Crenshaw/LAX (K) Line. Unlike the GTFS-sourced 2026 segment, these older headway numbers are not derived from real historical timetables and should be read as illustrative estimates, not precise data.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
